data.name: Mayuransh
data.long_meaning: Mayuransh is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Mayura' which means peacock. In Hindu mythology, the peacock is considered the vehicle of Lord Murugan, also known as Kartikeya, the God of War. The name Mayuransh signifies the power, strength, and grace associated with the peacock and the deity it represents.

historical_references.reference: Mayuransh was a Yadav king in ancient India, who is mentioned in the Mahabharata epic. He was a king of Haihayas, a branch of the Yadavas, and ruled over the kingdom of Magadha.

historical_references.reference: Mayuransh was also a name of King Mahendra, the legendary founder of the ancient Shiva temple at Pattadakal, in present-day Karnataka, India. The temple was built around 8th century CE and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
